releases.displayName: A Step Into the Zone – With 45% Off and Quality of Life Update

items.text: Hello Liquidators!

If you haven’t had the chance to step into the boots of a liquidator yet, now’s the perfect time to experience the gritty reality of a post-disaster world and join those who risked everything to contain the unthinkable.
We have prepared a quality of life update (v1.2.34). Check out the detailed list down below:
Added radiation sound when player is in radiation range
Increased range and visibility of where radiation warning flags should be placed
Increased range from which radiation warning flags can be buried
Increased the size of the task tracker - now contains more information about the task
Increased quality of some textures, e.g. radio
Increased speed of ozonation of radioactive clouds
Increased fire extinguishing speed
Increased player flashlight angle
Death screen changed
Memory optimizations
If you want to downgrade a game version for a while in case of some problems or game-breaking glitches, here’s the code for the branch -> prevChornobylBuild
This week also marks the anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster – a moment in history that continues to resonate around the world.
It’s a time to reflect on the real-life events behind the story, and to remember the people whose lives were forever changed.
Wish you a great time playing the game!
Cheers!
~Jacob and Developers

releases.displayName: Long-awaited update is finally here! Enjoy the game with the new VHS mode!

items.text: Early access to the new patch is over! We’re finally ready to push it fully public! We hope you’ll be enjoying the visual changes to the game and many smaller improvements.

We’ve introduced an additional option in the game settings that allows you to turn the VHS filter onto your game. We’ve tried to capture the soul of ‘80 and make the game more immersive with these on. You can now also adjust the brightness. Take a look for yourself!

We’ve also enabled the level selection for all players from the beginning of the game! You no longer need to finish the game to unlock it. You must finish all the maps to see the ending corresponding to your in-game choices. But if, for any reason, you want to skip a map or replay a certain one to see a different ending, you can now do that!
By the way, we added a tiny extra level -> Not great, not terrible :D

We’ve also prepared a special branch for you to jump into if you want to downgrade a game version for a while in case of some problems or game-breaking glitches. We upgraded to a newer version of the engine, a lot of things have changed, we fixed and tested everything, but we prepared it in case something went wrong.
Here’s the code for the branch -> prevChornobylBuild

That’s all for today. We hope to see some new faces on our Discord. We look forward to any feedback you may have for us after this new update. As always, thank you for your continued support of our games, and we look forward to hearing from you!
Cheers!
~Jacob and Developers

releases.displayName: Chornobyl Liquidators Release Date Trailer Update!

items.text: We know it's been a hot minute since the last devlog, but guess what? Today, we've got something really special cooking up for y'all! We've got a hefty dose of updates that'll definitely pique your interest. We've been grinding away these past months to gear up for what's finally upon us. Hope y'all are ready!
But without keeping you waiting any longer, let me spill the beans:
Mark your calendars, for June 6th, 2024, when we're dropping the launch of Chornobyl Liquidators! Set your alarms, gear up, 'cause we're diving into the Chornobyl disaster zone to lend a hand.
In the light of the big announcement, we've got a fresh-off-the-press trailer. Suit up in your radiation gear, because we're headed straight for the Chornobyl disaster zone.

Now that the dust has settled, we've got one more major piece of news . After days of negotiations, we've inked a deal with our friends over at Frozen Way, and they're going to become the publisher for Chornobyl Liquidators! We're stoked about this and looking forward to some fruitful collabs.
Wrapping it up slowly to leave you craving for more, we've whipped up some unique screenshots straight from ground zero.
Wrapping up for today, we want to extend a huge thank you for your patience throughout this journey. We're now rounding the final corner, and none of this would've been possible without you!
Stay safe, Liquidators!
Fufu and the Live Motion Games developers~

Thank you for being a part of our community and for your continued support. We hope you enjoy the improved gameplay experience!

notes.title: Thank you for playing our demo! We are happy to introduce some changes based on the feedback we've collected up until now - make sure to check them below!

items.text: As we receive a lot of very valuable feedback we do what we can to make sure that the demo version of our game is as polished as possible. We're introducing further changes designed to make sure that your enjoyment is increased and to ensure that your experience with the game is better.
One thing however does not change - we still await your feedback and can't wait to hear from you regarding your feeling after playing through the demo - now improved!
Player will no longer be immortal after the pulsating reactor sequence
Vision will no longer be improperly blurred after certain actions
Tutorial infographics have been reinstated and are properly translated to all languages
It is no longer possible to exit the playable area near the end of the demo
All player tasks and waypoints are now properly translated to all languages
Game now warns about high RAM demand of certain settings
Fixed issue with player being able to pickup some redundant items
Fixed issue with checkpoint inside the elevator shaft not being registered properly
Numerous player path and collision fixes
Minor tweaks to audio mastering
Kind regards,
Chernobyl Liquidators Simulator Team

notes.title: Welcome to the second part of our UI showcase. This time we'll talk more about the meaning behind those various icons you were able to see last time.

items.text: To make sure that our players can easily and painlessly enter the world of the game we've decided to prepare some extra info-graphics that will be displayed to you as you play through the game. We will talk more about them in our next devlog - stay tuned for that - but in this one we want to continue our last chat about the icons and UI. Some of the info-graphics will be conveying the most important aspects of the icons in a short and concise way to give you all the information required to survive in the harsh and unforgiving reality of Chernobyl.

We want to make sure that explanation for the particular icons in-game will be short but sweet - just a second needed to look over them to understand what is happening on the screen and to understand their purpose. Our UI designers are also working really hard to make sure that each of the symbols on your screen is easily recognized - for example red cross with a number under it symbolizes the number of health items available to you while the water tank is... basically a water tank!

Small icons on the right side of the screen (top to bottom): damage resistance, speed up, stamina regeneration, health recovery, health regeneration (over time) and their corresponding negative effects.

Fire, spillage, radiation - those are the big three of our icons and they will let you know not only what is happening in the area and what kind of danger you are dealing with but also the degree of the threat that you're facing and whether you're still within a safe area.

The smaller icons that you've seen in the last devlog will be a visual addition to the effects of certain items that you'll be able to use in-game. We hope that their design will help you in getting used to the effects and soon enough, after some time, you'll not have to read the effects but will simply be able to glance at the icons and instinctively know what they do.
Kind regards,
Chernobyl Liquidators Simulator Team

notes.title: We're coming back to the topic of UI - this time let's talk about radial menu and icons.

items.text: We have discussed the topic of UI previously - at that time we focused on the menus concerning the hints and dialogue boxes. However that is only a part of the grand scheme of things - UI is multilayered as our game is a little bit more complex and featuring tools and collectables system makes it necessary to design a neat UI and menu tailored especially for that particular feature. At the same time we want to make certain areas of the game more clear - to this effect we've been designing specific icons that will be easy and quick to understand.

Radial menu that we've prepared is designed to provide you with all the important information about the items and objects that you've collected throughout your gameplay. Not only all of them will receive an icon that will resemble the original object but you will also be able to read a short description of each of the objects and you'll be informed in a concise way about the effects of each of the items. This way you can make snap decision in the heat of a moment but if you have a moment of time and want to read the actual description - that is also completely fine!

We're also happy to present you with the icons that you will see in the game. Some of them you've already seen in the video above, some might be completely new to you. We'll be happy to discuss more about them in our next devlog - up until then we're wondering if you will be able to tell us what they might mean? If you could let us know in the comments what do you think they represent we will appreciate that a lot - it will also be a test of sorts for us to check if they are as transparent as we believe them to be.
Kind regards,
Chernobyl Liquidators Simulator Team

notes.title: Thank you very much for your participation in the playtest - as we continue the testing we are also happy to introduce few fixes and adjustment to the current version of the game!

items.text: Over 30.000 players have participated in the playtest up until this moment. We are honoured by the reception our tests received and we intend to continue gathering feedback from you as we believe your voice is what truly matters! We are sure that by incoporating your thoughts and ideas within our game we can truly create something unique!
At the current moment we are very happy to introduce a patch to the playtest version of the game based exactly on your feedback. Below you can read what exactly has been changed and improved.
HELP screens added - available at all the times by pressing F1 or GAMEPAD SELECT buttons
Mouse sensitivity slider is working properly now
Toggle sprint option is working properly no (it is recommended to disable it for GAMEPAD control)
Additional details were added to environment and reactor ruins
Firetrucks are properly scaled now (non-mirrored textures with proper lettering coming soon)
Audio of interactions should now play for a longer time if player died in between them
Timing of audio during the ladder climb cinematic has been properly synchronized with animation
We still strongly encourage you to send us as much feedback as you can as it can directly influence the game development and it helps us out a lot.
Kind regards,
Chernobyl Liquidators Simulator Team
